OSS COMPARISON OF REBAR'S JIRA DATA CENTER INTEGRATION — findings, remediation, and what was NOT
verifiable. Commissioned to check that our integration follows a well-trodden path and that any
divergence is intentional.

=== THE HEADLINE: ONE DEFECT THAT WRITES WRONG DATA ===

[rebar:21fc-51d7-90ca-4a03] DC INDEX LAG MAKES recover_pending CREATE DUPLICATE ISSUES. Verified in
source, not taken on trust. binding_store.py:521-531, keyless-pending branch, searches JQL for the
rebar-id label and UNBINDS when the search returns nothing — its docstring says 'unbind if not (the
create never reached Jira)'. But keyless-pending is entered PRECISELY when we crashed during
create_issue, and DC's Lucene index is explicitly eventually consistent (Atlassian KB; JRASERVER-70423
documents an index 2,991 seconds — ~50 min — behind). A JQL search cannot see an unindexed issue, so
on a lagging cluster recovery concludes the create never landed, unbinds, and the NEXT PASS CREATES A
DUPLICATE.
The authors already understood this hazard: the KEYED branch's docstring says 'NO Jira search —
deterministic, so a hard crash in the create->label window yields NO duplicate.' They engineered it
away where a key was known. The keyless branch had to search, and search is the index-dependent
operation. Sound on Cloud, unsound on DC.
This is the ONLY finding in the whole review where rebar writes wrong data rather than reading
incomplete data. Ranked must-fix.

=== FIXED IMMEDIATELY, IN THE CHANGE THAT WAS STILL IN REVIEW ===

PAGINATION TRUNCATION in get_parent_map — a data-loss bug in code I had pushed twenty minutes earlier.
DC silently truncates maxResults above jira.search.views.default.max (Atlassian's REST reference and
maxResults KB both say so; a common hardening). My loop advanced by the REQUESTED page size and broke
on a short page, so a truncated FIRST page read as 'that is all there is'. Measured with a client
capping pages at 20: 20 of 250 parents recovered — 92% silently lost, raising nothing, and the inbound
pass would treat every unseen issue as parentless.
Fixed in change 1105 by advancing by len(batch) and breaking only on an EMPTY page, with a held-out
regression test. Amended rather than filed as follow-up because the change had not landed.

=== FILED FOR FOLLOW-UP ===

[rebar:b586-2fda-8a15-4260] Rate limiting. DC-only, 8.6+, and OFF BY DEFAULT (admin-enabled), a
per-user token bucket. So a static pacing policy is NOT implementable — the whole fix is to honour
retry-after when present and degrade when absent. Atlassian prescribes retry-after PLUS up to 20%
random jitter, which differs from rebar's ADR-0036 backoff curve.

[rebar:387d-09c5-3d50-4a1e] A failed identity write DELETES the created issue. The mature answer is
NOT to solve field discovery: Sentry's Jira integration explicitly declares it does not support custom
required fields ('The only required fields supported are those that are pre-populated by Sentry').
Remediation is (1) stop deleting — a created-but-unlabelled issue is recoverable via retro-attach, a
deleted one is not; (2) document the labels-on-screen requirement; (3) defer createmeta, possibly
forever. Note the Jira error 'not on the appropriate screen' is misleading roughly half the time — it
also fires from the workflow property jira.permission.createclone.denied and from a MALFORMED value on
a field that IS on the screen.

[rebar:7c26-4ac8-04a3-440e] Bindings key on the Jira KEY, which changes on project move (the numeric id
never does). DC-specific KB: third-party apps moving issues via post-functions/automations can fail to
update the moved_issue_key table, after which the old key stops resolving entirely.

=== EPISTEMIC NOTE — the research corrected ITSELF, and I am recording what stayed unverified ===

The agent's second pass RETRACTED two claims its first pass had stated firmly. I am recording that
rather than quietly adopting the stronger version:
 * What GET /rest/api/2/issue/{oldKey} returns for a moved issue (200-with-new-key vs 301 vs 404) is
   NOT established. The remediation (key on id) stands regardless; only the DETECTION mechanism is
   unverified, and 7c26 carries an operator-attested AC to settle it on the harness.
 * The 'max.limit < default.max causes 403' claim is documented for search VIEWS, not for
   /rest/api/2/search. TRUNCATION by default.max IS well-supported. The pagination fix is correct
   under either reading, which is why it was safe to land.
Still unresolved across both passes: PAT default expiry (one pass says 365-day max with a 10-token
cap, the other says expiry is optional and defaults to none — likely version-dependent); whether
PATs authenticate attachment retrieval (community-sourced only; rebar handles no attachments today);
whether 'total' on DC v2 is clamped (which is why the fix drives the loop off the returned page, not
off total).

=== CONVERGENCE: where we match the community, and where we do not ===

The comparison did not overturn the epic's core design decisions. pycontribs/jira as the DC client,
PAT bearer auth, and an ephemeral Docker harness as the verification oracle are all consistent with
what mature projects do — and the rejected PR that hand-rolled a REST v2 client would have diverged
from that consensus, not toward it.
What this review DID find is that our divergences are mostly not in the architecture but in the
OPERATIONAL EDGES that only show up against a real, differently-configured instance: index lag,
server-side pagination caps, admin-toggled rate limiting, screen configuration, project moves. That is
a coherent pattern and worth stating plainly in J8's ADR: the seam design held up; the gaps were all
in assuming a Cloud-shaped instance behaves like a DC-shaped one.

=== WHAT THIS SAYS ABOUT THE METHOD ===

Every one of these was invisible to 1693 passing unit tests, a certified plan, and two green plan
reviews. Two were invisible to the live harness as well, because the harness is a single
default-configured 8.17.1 instance — it does not have a lagging index, a lowered
jira.search.views.default.max, rate limiting enabled, or a restricted create screen. So 'live testing
is the oracle' is necessary and still not sufficient: the oracle only covers the configurations the
oracle happens to have.

=== HANDOFF #4 — epic e369 (Jira Server/Data Center). READ FIRST. ===

BOARD (verified, not remembered)
  e369 epic        in_progress
  8c35 J8  story   IN_PROGRESS, claimed. ADR 0055 MERGED (change 1107). Ready to CLOSE.
  bda8 J9  story   IN_PROGRESS, claimed. All code MERGED (1105/1106/1108). Live-verified. Ready to CLOSE.
  bb8c J10 story   CLOSED certified.
  5200 J11 story   OPEN. Plan at review round 4 (rounds 1-3 blocked; all findings now fixed).
  b586     story   OPEN. Rate limiter, now IN SCOPE by operator direction.
  21fc 387d 7c26 9263 f391  bugs OPEN — see 'defect-free' below.
  a357     bug     OPEN — implemented BY bda8; close when bda8 closes.
  6a91 cc77 dbf9 06e0 — open, deliberately OUT of this epic.

WORKTREE /Users/joeoakhart/rebar-jira-family @ 8ffdcea0d, clean. ALWAYS: export PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH"

THE STANDARD THE OPERATOR SET: 'the implicit acceptance criteria is shipping defect free code.' That
is why 387d and 7c26 are IN scope despite being pre-existing and not DC-specific — shipping DC support
ships those paths to a new deployment type. My earlier 'pre-existing therefore follow-up' framing was
retired; the live Cloud bridge escapes both only because its trigger conditions (permanent
identity-write failure; project moves) do not occur there, not because Cloud is immune.

WHAT IS PROVEN, AND WHAT IS NOT
 * PROVEN LIVE: a DC writing pass converges cleanly — 'OK: steady-state pass converged' on a real
   instance, no traceback (CI run 30637886718).
 * NOT PROVEN: that data MOVES. That run reported scanned=0 — it converged because the store was
   EMPTY. The epic's headline operator-attested AC (an issue created in DC appears locally; a local
   edit appears in DC) has NO evidence. J11 exists to get it. Do not close the epic on 'converged'.

REMAINING TO CLOSE THE EPIC: close 8c35 and bda8 (both ready); land J11 (live proof); b586; and the
four shipped-code defects 21fc, 387d, 7c26, 9263 — plus f391 FIRST, because J11 runs on a harness that
currently dies at setup on the 10-PAT cap.

HARD-WON, EXPENSIVE LESSONS — these cost real time, please carry them
 1. COUNTS ARE NOT CAUSES. All three live runs reported '2 failed, 12 passed, 1 error' with three
    DIFFERENT causes. Read the error text every time.
 2. ABSENCE OF ERRORS IS NOT EVIDENCE OF FUNCTION. 7 of the 12 transport members were swallowed by
    'except Exception' at every call site; 'nothing raised' was true while nothing worked.
 3. WHEN A PLAN KEEPS RETURNING DOUBLE-DIGIT FINDINGS, SUSPECT STRUCTURE. J9 blocked 8 times; splitting
    the exception contract into J10 produced a first-try PASS.
 4. AFTER EDITING A PLAN, GREP THE WHOLE DOCUMENT FOR THE TERM YOU CHANGED. Six BLOCK rounds came from
    revising the analysis and leaving Scope or the ACs stale. Once I introduced a contradiction while
    fixing the very thing it contradicted.
 5. ON FINDING A DEFECT CLASS, SWEEP FOR SIBLINGS. I fixed pagination in get_parent_map and left the
    same bug in get_issuelinks_map and get_comment_map (9263).
 6. VERIFY MECHANISMS, NOT PLAUSIBILITY. I twice asserted a mechanism I had not traced — 'prev_snapshot
    drives mass deletion' (it is a baseline store for bound tickets) and 'the local harness fails on
    resource contention' (the README documents arm64 emulation; the image is linux/amd64 only).
 7. LIVE TESTING IS THE ORACLE — AND STILL NOT SUFFICIENT. The harness is ONE default-configured
    8.17.1 instance: no index lag, no lowered page cap, no rate limiting, no restricted screens. Every
    OSS-comparison finding was invisible to it.
 8. pycontribs/jira is the AUTHORITATIVE interface; its API is SPLIT across jira.JIRA and
    jira.resources.Issue, and @translate_resource_args defeats STATIC lookup — verify at runtime.

MECHANICS: plan-review certified BEFORE claim; review-plan FAST-FAILS on a blocked ticket; editing a
plan stales its attestation; SERIALIZE LLM gates (one review or one close at a time); Gerrit needs
LLM-Review +1 AND Verified +1 then POST /a/changes/<n>/submit -d '{}'; Gerrit REBASES on submit so
verify landed CONTENT then 'git reset --hard origin/main'; commits need 50-char subject / 72-col body,
a rebar-ticket trailer, -s, and the venv on PATH.

=== HANDOFF #5 — epic e369 (Jira Server/Data Center). READ AFTER #4. ===

WORKTREE /Users/joeoakhart/rebar-jira-family, branch jira-family-seam @ 3 commits above 8ffdcea0d.
ALWAYS: export PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH"

THREE CORRECTIONS TO HANDOFF #4 — it said 8c35 and bda8 were "ready to CLOSE". NEITHER WAS.

 1. bda8's close returned SEVEN unmet criteria. Six were genuinely missing work, now implemented and
    pushed (change 1113): the construction-time conformance guard did not exist at all — the port
    declared the members and NOTHING checked them where a backend is built, so `isinstance` returning
    False in a test was a demonstration that a guard was possible, not a guard. Added
    `assert_transport_conforms()` and wired it into BOTH factories (Cloud too: the port states what
    the CORE requires). Verified both real transports satisfy it BEFORE relying on it, so the guard
    cannot make a shipped backend unbuildable — that check is itself now a test. Plus four tests:
    reporter idempotence via the real `_identity_of`, `set_entity_property` key/value integrity, a
    `caplog` assertion that the WARNING actually FIRES, and `validate_assignee_exists` raising
    `AssigneeNotFoundError` specifically. ALL FOUR MUTATION-CHECKED (removing each guard call,
    blanking `logger.warning`, deleting `_diff_reporter`'s early return -> exactly the expected
    failures).
    The 7th criterion ("`git diff` shows test_reconcile_pass.py unchanged") was UNMEETABLE: that
    file's writing-mode assertions called `_envelope()`, and `__main__.py:444-452` shows only the
    `no_write` branch emits JSON — the assertion could never have passed and was masked by the
    crash-on-missing-member. The operator authorised remediating it; it is now three verifiable
    properties (no assertion deleted without a still-failing replacement; envelope-emitting modes
    keep their assertions; every change cites the emitting code) instead of a git-diff invariant.

 2. 8c35's close returned one unmet criterion, correctly: the guide's commands had NEVER been run.
    Change 1115 adds `tests/external/live_jira_dc/test_user_guide_commands.py`, which PARSES the
    config block out of `docs/user-guide.md` at runtime — a restated copy would keep passing while
    the doc rotted. Writes a pyproject.toml, because `[tool.rebar.reconciler]` is the pyproject
    surface (`_config_sources.py:111-115`) while `rebar.toml` takes bare `[reconciler]`; the existing
    live module uses the OTHER form, so reusing its fixture would have proven the guide by not using
    it. Asserts a `no_write` envelope, the extra really exists, and that JIRA_PAT is env-only (PAT in
    config + absent from env MUST fail naming the variable — the guide sells that as a security
    property).

 3. PREFIX COLLISIONS. `f391` and `b586` each match TWO tickets. Use f391-806b-938f-45d8 (PAT cap)
    and b586-2fda-8a15-4260 (rate limiter).

f391 IS FIXED (change 1114). `jira_dc_pat` is session-scoped (O(1) tokens, not O(tests)) plus a
session-start sweep of leftover `rebar-j5-harness-*` PATs. The sweep ONLY touches that prefix — the
admin account may hold a human's PATs and deleting one to reclaim budget would be worse than the bug;
that exclusion is a test with teeth (incl. a prefix-adjacent name that must NOT match). 13 unit tests
against a stubbed `_request`; the scope fix is mutation-checked.

NEW DEFECT FOUND AND FILED — [rebar:deac-4f5a-856a-49bd], THE THIRD SIBLING.
`fetcher._iter_pages` (fetcher.py:324-326) stops on a SHORT page and advances by the REQUESTED size —
identical to the `get_parent_map` bug fixed in 1105. REPRODUCED, not inferred: a client serving 250
issues while capping pages at 20 yields 20. **92% of the inbound snapshot silently lost.** Worse than
9263: `collect()` feeds `_build_snapshot`, so it loses THE ISSUES THEMSELVES, and every unseen bound
issue becomes a candidate for the deletion path. NOT folded into 9263 deliberately — 9263 is
adapter-local, this is CORE on the shared Cloud path, so it needs its own review and its own proof
the Cloud contract (cap / ACLI ceiling / same-token-twice) is unchanged.

21fc's OWN REMEDIATION IS WRONG — corrected on the ticket, plan not yet rewritten.
There are TWO index-dependent sites, and 21fc names only the first:
  1. `recover_pending` keyless branch — unbinds on a negative search (the site 21fc describes);
  2. `create_one`'s JQL dedup (dispatch_one.py:237-238) — on a miss it CREATES. THIS is what writes
     the duplicate.
Fixing only site 1 does NOT help: `outbound_differ.py:528-531` gates the create on
`get_jira_key(local_id) is None`, and a keyless-pending entry HAS `jira_key: None`
(binding_store.py:258-262), so the create is emitted anyway and the dedup misses for the same
index-lag reason. `is_pending()` exists (binding_store.py:270) and the differ does not consult it.
THE FIX MUST BE AT THE CREATE GATE: defer the create while a keyless-pending binding is inside an
index-lag grace window. The AC must drive the WHOLE path (crash -> recover -> differ -> create) under
a lagging client and assert EXACTLY ONE issue created; a test asserting only "recover_pending did not
unbind" passes while the duplicate is still written.

J11 (5200) — ROUND 4 BLOCKED, 7 findings, ALL FIXED IN THE PLAN. And it produced a SEQUENCING result:
**5200 now depends_on deac, so J11 cannot be claimed until the pagination defects land** — the gate
agrees with the finding. The pagination AC ("seed 2*observed+1") is MEANINGLESS while 9263 and deac
stand: seeding past the page size would silently truncate and report a converged pass over a fraction
of the data — the exact green-but-broken outcome J11 exists to end.
Two findings corrected MY errors, both verified in source before accepting:
  * `prev_snapshot` is the OUTBOUND field-change baseline (`OutboundDiffConfig.prev_snapshot`), so a
    leftover production copy produces a wave of spurious outbound UPDATEs — NOT deletions. The AC now
    asserts zero deletions AND <10 outbound updates, because a deletion-only assertion passes at a
    reassuring zero while the run is corrupted in the way that actually happens. (This is the THIRD
    restatement of this file's role in the plan; it is now stated from the code path.)
  * `set_parent`'s NotImplementedError is SWALLOWED by `dispatch_one.py:564`, so asserting it through
    the reconciler subprocess is untestable by construction. It must be asserted directly against the
    transport.
  * the "no production Jira key reference" AC was MECHANICALLY UNACHIEVABLE — ticket event files
    legitimately embed `jira_key` from prior Cloud syncs and the scrub correctly leaves them. Replaced
    with `.bridge_state*` scrub completeness.
I ALSO RAN LESSON 4 (grep the whole document after editing) AND IT CAUGHT A REAL CONTRADICTION: the
Approach opener listed "pagination" among defects the store copy surfaces, while the volume bullet
says pagination is remote-side and the copy does not exercise it. Fixed. That habit works — use it.

REVISED ORDER (changed by the above): deac + 9263 FIRST (they gate J11's evidence), THEN J11, THEN
21fc (with the corrected two-site fix), 387d, 7c26, b586.

IN FLIGHT: changes 1113/1114/1115 awaiting LLM-Review +1 and Verified +1. deac's plan review running.

ENVIRONMENT WARNINGS
 * ANOTHER AGENT SESSION runs concurrently in /Users/joeoakhart/rebar-wt-provider-seam (ticket 7f86).
   It competes for CPU and for LLM gates and it pushes to main. The unit suite took 24 MINUTES under
   that contention. Expect it; do not diagnose it as a code problem.
 * DO NOT run a full `pytest tests/unit` while committing — 7 "Test moved the repo HEAD" ERRORS in
   this session were caused by my own commits landing mid-run, not by defects. Counts are not causes.
 * A test placed in `tests/external/live_jira_dc/` WITHOUT a harness skipif does NOT run harness-free:
   the session-scoped autouse `_jira_dc_harness_ready` waits out the full 20-minute budget and then
   errors (measured 1208s), and `tests/unit/test_external_isolation.py` FAILS the build for it. Put
   repo-only checks in `tests/unit/`.

=== HANDOFF #6 — epic e369 (Jira Server/Data Center). READ THIS AND #5. ===

WORKTREE /Users/joeoakhart/rebar-jira-family, branch jira-family-seam @ 13ddc3bed, clean.
ALWAYS: export PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH"

*** THE BIG RESULT: THE INBOUND HALF OF THE HEADLINE AC IS PROVEN. THE OUTBOUND HALF IS NOT. ***

Run 30662366152 (job "jira DC harness smoke", main @ ed9d5e28d): collected=17 executed=17 skipped=0,
**17 passed** — the first FULLY GREEN DC harness run in this epic.
`test_a_dc_created_ticket_carries_the_shared_jira_provenance` passes: an issue created in DC appears
in the local store with id == `_jira_key_to_local_id(remote_key)` AND the binding store mapping that
id to the DC key.

THE OUTBOUND HALF REMAINS UNPROVEN, and I checked rather than assumed:
`tests/external/live_jira_dc/test_reconcile_pass.py` has exactly three live tests and NONE mutates a
local ticket then asserts the change surfaces on the DC issue. [rebar:5200] (J11) must supply it.
**DO NOT CLOSE THE EPIC UNTIL IT DOES.**

WHY THIS TOOK SO LONG TO SEE — three defects masked it in sequence, each hiding the next:
  1. an EMPTY store made the pass report scanned=0 and "converged" — indistinguishable from working;
  2. the PAT-cap bug killed the suite at SETUP before the test ran;
  3. the ORACLE ITSELF COULD NOT PASS — it grepped the raw key `RBJ...-1` against a payload whose id
     is lowercased `jira-rbj...-1` and which carries no raw key at all.
Only with all three fixed does that test's verdict carry information. Its earlier RED was not evidence
of breakage, and a green before the fix would not have been evidence of function.

BOARD
  CLOSED this session: f391-806b-938f-45d8, bda8-370d-23ad-4e36 (J9), a357, 23ed-de0a-765b-49aa,
    deac-4f5a-856a-49bd, 0059-c7f0-cce1-4077 (duplicate), 2bc7-d77b-641c-42aa (preexisting).
  MERGED to main: bda8(1113) f391(1114) 8c35(1115) deac(1118) 23ed(1124) cd78(1127).
  IN REVIEW, all three LLM-Review +1 awaiting Verified: 1129 (9263 shared pager), 1130 (21fc duplicate

  READY TO CLOSE NOW (evidence already recorded on both): 8c35-1a5e-927b-4644 and

  STILL OPEN under e369: 5200 (J11), 5f48, 7c26 (plan CERTIFIED, ready to claim), b586 (plan written,

REPARENTED BUGS — DISPOSITION (operator asked me to wire these in)

  * 2bc7 "unregistered copy of mutation.py" — CLOSED as preexisting. WE OWNED IT on file overlap: all
    three of its declared files were last modified by 199b637b5 ("0a94: pin a UserIdentityModel

  * 5f48 "DC inbound identity mint fails silently ('jira-datacenter' is not a valid creation_channel)"
    — IN SCOPE, PROVEN by measurement, and I added **5200 depends_on 5f48**. RATIONALE: J11 exists to
    prove data moves; a SILENTLY SWALLOWED inbound identity failure is exactly the class of defect that
    would let J11 report success over broken behaviour. Fix 5f48 before trusting J11's evidence.
  * cc77 "transport params untyped" — IN SCOPE; added cc77 relates_to bda8. It is the STATIC (mypy)
    complement to the RUNTIME conformance guard bda8 added. Was on the old "outside this epic" list;

  * fe15 "duplicated local->Jira value maps, already drifted" — in scope (Jira adapter work), no extra
    edge needed.

RECOMMENDED ORDER FROM HERE
  1. Close 8c35 and cd78 (evidence recorded; one LLM gate at a time).
  2. Land 1129/1130/1131 as their Verified votes arrive; then close 9263, 21fc, 387d.
     BEFORE closing 21fc: its plan says the create gate lives in outbound_differ. It does NOT — the
     module-size cap forced it into dispatch_one.create_one (a better site: guards the WRITE and
     reuses deferred_creates). Update the plan's Approach + that AC and record why, or the close fails
     on a stale plan.
  3. Fix 5f48 (it gates J11's credibility), then 7c26 (plan certified), then b586 (needs review).
  4. J11 (5200) LAST — it is the outbound proof and the epic's closing condition.
  5. cc77 and fe15 can land any time; neither blocks the headline.

HARD-WON LESSONS FROM THIS SESSION (all cost real time)
 1. `rebar comment` is POSITIONAL: `rebar comment <id> <body>`. There is NO --body flag — passing one
    records the literal string "--body" AND EXITS 0. SIX evidence comments were silently lost this way,
    and I only noticed because a close gate correctly said the attestation was missing. VERIFY every
    comment landed (`rebar show <id>`, check byte length). Do not trust the exit code or your own echo.
 2. A CLOSE FAILS IF THE EVIDENCE IS NOT ON THE TICKET, even when the CI run exists. Record run id +
    job name + the specific test verdicts BEFORE attempting a close.
 3. LOCAL PYTEST IS NOT A FAITHFUL CI ORACLE HERE. CI runs py3.11; this host has only 3.13/3.14.
    Python 3.12 changed runtime-checkable Protocol isinstance from `hasattr` to
    `inspect.getattr_static`, so a PROPERTY THAT RAISES breaks isinstance on 3.11 while passing
    locally. That earned a Verified -1 on cd78 and is why its guard lives in
    build_client_from_settings, not in settings resolution. When touching anything a property calls,
    assert via `hasattr` directly so the test is interpreter-independent.
 4. PRE-PUSH GATES, all of which bit: (a) module size — cap 800, LOCKED, no allowlist, and
    outbound_differ.py sits at EXACTLY 800 on main so NOTHING may be added to it; check EACH COMMIT
    independently. (b) env-var registry — docs/env-vars.md is GENERATED and records LINE NUMBERS, so
    any insertion above an env read drifts it: run `python scripts/gen_env_registry.py`. (c) commit
    subject <= 50 chars (a 52-char subject was rejected), body wrapped at 72.
 5. DIAGNOSE CI VIA THE FAILING STEP, not log greps: `gh run view <id> --repo navapbc/rebar --json
    jobs`. Log text echoes the workflow SCRIPT (including its `::error::` lines) and will send you
    after the wrong cause — it did exactly that to me on 21fc's second failure.
 6. FOUR EXISTING TESTS ENCODED DEFECTS this session (the `_envelope()` writing-mode oracle, the
    unbind-after-one-miss assertion, and three delete_issue-was-called rollback assertions). When an
    existing test blocks a fix, CHECK WHETHER IT PINS THE BUG; if so invert it preserving its INTENT
    and record why in the docstring. That is not oracle-fitting — leaving it would be.
 7. VERIFY AN ORACLE CAN PASS before trusting its RED or its GREEN — including your own new
    assertions. I nearly shipped a fourth unpassable oracle; `list_tickets` returns `ticket_id`, not
    `id`, and I checked before relying on it.
 8. `git commit --amend -F -` REGENERATES the Change-Id (forking a duplicate Gerrit change) and can
    sweep other staged files into the wrong commit. Use `--amend --no-edit` and verify the Change-Id.
 9. Bare 4-hex prefixes are often AMBIGUOUS (f391, b586, 23ed, 2bc7 all match two tickets). Use FULL
    ids. The "Error: Ambiguous prefix ..." lines in close output are harmless stderr noise from a
    merged commit's subject — read PAST them for the real result.
 10. ANOTHER AGENT SESSION runs concurrently in /Users/joeoakhart/rebar-wt-provider-seam. It competes
    for CPU and LLM gates and pushes to main. A full local tests/unit/rebar_reconciler run TIMED OUT at
    25 minutes under that contention — run targeted modules and let Gerrit's Verified gate be the
    authoritative suite signal.

`test_a_dc_issue_reaches_the_local_store_inbound` FAILS live. Latest: run 30699907628, job
91368976778. 1 failed, 23 passed. The pass prints:

  RECON: outbound_differ total=1639 create=1639 update=0 delete=0
  RECON: inbound_differ total=0 with_fields=0 with_labels=0 with_comments=0
  filter: 1640 mutations computed, 0 match filter (1 local IDs, 1 target keys)
  RECON: typed_inbound_dispatched count=0 suppressed_pairs=0

The DC issue is created, then a `bootstrap-strict` pass scoped with
`--filter-local-ids jira-<key>` is run, and the local ticket never appears.

ALREADY RULED OUT — do NOT re-test these, each cost a full harness cycle (~8 min + review + merge):

    it was module-local to test_transport.py. MOVED to conftest.py (change 1159). Note
    `pytest --collect-only` does NOT catch this; fixtures resolve at SETUP. Use
    `pytest --fixtures <module>` instead.
 2. THE STORE WAS NOT A GIT REPO. Second failure: `binding-store commit to tickets branch failed
    (CalledProcessError(128, ['git','-C','.../.tickets-tracker','commit',...]))`. 128 = "not a git
    repository". `.tickets-tracker/` IS its own repo on the orphan `tickets` branch and the
    reconciler commits into it directly. Fixed in 1161: the tracker gets its own `git init -b
    tickets`, committed AFTER the scrub; the outer repo gitignores it; BOTH get a local committer
    identity (a CI runner has no global one).
 3. INDEX LAG — **HYPOTHESIS DISPROVEN, and I was wrong to assume it.** I added

    fails loudly naming index lag. The latest run did NOT fail that way, so the poll SUCCEEDED:
    the issue WAS searchable and `inbound_differ` still saw nothing. Index lag is not the cause.
    Keep the helper — it is correct and the pagination cell needs it — but stop attributing this
    failure to it.

FACTS GATHERED, so the next session starts from evidence rather than guesses:
 * The fetcher's inbound JQL is a PAIR (fetcher.py:69-81): `project = <KEY> AND status != "Done"`
   and `project = <KEY> AND status = "Done" ORDER BY updated DESC`. A new Task is not Done, so
   jql_active SHOULD match it. `_validate_project_key` interpolates the key UNQUOTED.
 * `--filter-local-ids` is a POST filter, not a scoping optimisation: "1640 mutations computed,
   0 match filter". The whole store is computed every pass. Isolation still held — 0 applied.
 * outbound_differ computing 1639 creates is EXPECTED and harmless here: the scrub removes every
   binding, so every copied ticket looks new (`outbound_differ.py:518-520` routes jira_key None to
   CREATE). The filter drops them all.

THE PRIME SUSPECT AND THE SAFE EXPERIMENT. It is not established whether the RECON counters are
printed before or after the filter is applied. If AFTER, then `inbound_differ total=0` is telling
us the FILTER removed the inbound create rather than that the differ never made one — and the
whole diagnosis flips. TEST IT WITHOUT MUTATING THE HARNESS: run the same pass as
`--mode dry-run` WITHOUT `--filter-local-ids` and inspect the envelope's `.plan` for an entry with
`direction == "inbound"` and `action == "create"` naming the key. Dry-run writes nothing, so the
1639 outbound creates cannot fire. Do NOT run an unfiltered WRITING pass — bootstrap-strict
(cap=10, mode.py:106) would file 10 production tickets into the harness, and `live` would file all
1639.
Second suspect if that comes back clean: compare against
`test_a_dc_created_ticket_carries_the_shared_jira_provenance` in test_reconcile_pass.py, which
does the same inbound round-trip and PASSES. The material differences are (a) it uses the
`rebar_repo` empty store, not a copied one, and (b) it runs UNFILTERED. Diffing those two cells is
probably the shortest path to the answer.

WHAT IS PROVEN GREEN LIVE (all three passed on every run since 1158):
 * `test_the_working_repo_is_isolated_from_this_project` — no remote on BOTH repos (the outer one
   AND the store repo, which is the one that would actually push), REBAR_SYNC_PUSH=off, no Cloud
   credential.
 * `test_the_store_copy_is_complete_and_scrubbed` — 2673 ticket entries extracted into
   `.tickets-tracker/`, count MATCHING `git ls-tree origin/tickets` exactly (a count comparison,
   not a `> 0` floor, so a PARTIAL extraction fails), and zero `.bridge_state*` survivors.
 * `test_the_scrubbed_copy_plans_no_deletions_or_outbound_updates` — zero deletions AND zero
   outbound updates over the real copy, confirming from a live instance the reasoning that an
   outbound UPDATE cannot be emitted without a binding.

J11's PLAN PASSED AFTER 12 ROUNDS and is SIGNED (head_sha 1895c987b8). Finding counts went
6,3,4,3,4,2,3,2,4,1,2,0. Do not reopen settled ACs. The three deepest corrections it produced:
 * `scanned` is `len(curr_snapshot)` — the count of REMOTE Jira issues (`reconcile.py:286`), NOT
   local tickets. So it can never prove the store copy is non-empty. **This also corrects handoff
   #4**, which read an early run's `scanned=0` as "the STORE was EMPTY"; on this code it means the
   HARNESS had no issues. The store-copy AC now counts tickets on the filesystem instead.
 * In DRY-RUN there is no `scanned=` line at all — `persist` is False, so it takes the skip branch
   and prints `invariants: skipped (no-write mode, <N> issues in snapshot)` to STDERR. Only an
   UNFILTERED WRITING pass prints `scanned=` to STDOUT. I got this wrong twice in the plan.
 * Outbound rows 2-13 are all UPDATEs and need a binding the scrub removes, so they share a
   `bound_dc_issue` fixture: create the DC issue, run a writing pass SCOPED with
   `--filter-local-ids jira-<dc_key.lower()>` (computable in advance because
   `_jira_key_to_local_id` is pure, `inbound_translate.py:120-124`), then mutate locally. There is
   NO inbound-only mode — every writing mode also runs the outbound differ — which is why that
   filter is mandatory.

REMAINING J11 WORK: fix the inbound cell, then the outbound round-trip + the `bound_dc_issue`
fixture, then the 28-cell mutation suite per the plan's oracle table, then pagination
(unfiltered DRY-RUN + poll until all seeded keys are searchable), then idempotence.

STANDING RULES — the three that bit hardest this session, added to the ones in #6/#7:
 * A `rebar edit`/`comment` CAN FAIL ON LOCK CONTENTION and the surrounding script still reports
   OK: `flock: could not acquire lock after 60s`. The other session
   (/Users/joeoakhart/rebar-wt-provider-seam) holds the store lock. ALWAYS re-read and compare
   LENGTH after a write; retry on mismatch.
 * THE GITHUB MIRROR LAGS GERRIT. After a submit, `origin/main` may not have the content for a
   minute or two — that is NOT a failed submit. Verify against `git fetch gerrit main` first, and
   wait for the mirror before dispatching a workflow that runs `--ref main`.
 * `pytest --collect-only` PROVES NOTHING ABOUT FIXTURES. They resolve at setup. Use
   `pytest --fixtures <module>`.
 * Don't background a long command with a bare `&` — it escapes harness task tracking and you get
   no completion notification. Use the proper background mechanism.

=== HANDOFF #18 ADDENDUM — a CI failure mode worth knowing, and its fix ===

**A change based on an older commit can fail CI on a step whose SCRIPT its tree does not contain — and
it looks nothing like a rebase problem.** 1276 (2b16) took `Verified -1` with:

    python: can't open file '/home/runner/work/rebar/rebar/scripts/check_config_reads.py':
    [Errno 2] No such file or directory
    ##[error]Process completed with exit code 2.

Diagnosis, and the part that misleads: `build-and-test` DID run (so it was NOT the concurrency-group
cancellation trap from #15/#17 — lint + type-check + pip-audit all passed and only the four pytest legs
failed), and there was no failing TEST at all. **CI takes the WORKFLOW from main but the CODE from the
patchset.** `3ad3abe72` ("6754: config-is-read gate for schema fields", change 1257) added
`.github/workflows/_build-and-test.yml:434 → python scripts/check_config_reads.py` AND
`scripts/check_config_reads.py` atomically. 1276 was based on `6cdd4b00d9`, which predates it, so the
workflow-from-main invoked a script the patchset tree lacked. Every older-based change in flight hits
this: 1279/1280 were based on `ba3c06ee47` and would have failed identically.

**Fix: REBASE. This is the #17 trap "Rebase-If-Necessary applies at SUBMIT, not to CI" in its most
confusing dress** — the symptom is a missing FILE, so it reads as a broken main rather than a stale base.
All three changes were rebased onto `gerrit/main` and re-pushed; the diff stat was checked against
`gerrit/main` each time to confirm nothing was swept in (4 files / 782 insertions for 1276; 3 files /
750 for the 1279+1280 stack), and `scripts/check_config_reads.py` now runs clean locally.

**A wrong turn I took, recorded so nobody repeats it:** I first checked for the script with
`git cat-file -e <ref>:scripts/check_config_reads.py` inside a `for` loop with `&&`/`||` chaining and got
"MISSING" for EVERY ref including current main — which made it look like main itself was broken for
everyone. That reading was wrong. `git ls-tree -r --name-only <ref> -- <path>` gave the correct answer
(present on main, absent on both older bases). **Use `ls-tree` for per-ref file existence**, and be
suspicious of a result that says the whole repo is broken.

**The `Missing tree <sha>` push error from #18 is fixable.** 2b16's agent hit it twice pushing a
rebased tree (including with `--no-thin`) and gave up, pushing from the original base — which is what
caused the CI failure above. Running a FULL `git fetch gerrit` (all refs, not `git fetch gerrit main`)
before the push made it succeed first try: the client then has the remote's objects and builds a valid
thin pack. Do that instead of abandoning the rebase.

operator caught it (they saw 7 in the epic they were closing; the true radius was 63). It was the
**PRODUCTION JIRA CLOUD bridge** (`reconcile-bridge.yml`, cron `*/20`) — so 88d9 was never a DC-only
change; it is shared core and Cloud is where it fired.

MECHANISM — AND IT IS THE SAME WRONG PREMISE AS 2b16, WHICH I HAD PROVEN HOURS EARLIER.
`diff_inbound_parent` cleared the local parent when the peer was OBSERVED parentless and the ref was in
`managed_refs`. But `add_managed_ref` is folded by the parent-set EVENT, so a ref is "managed" the
instant it is set LOCALLY — managed NEVER proved the peer had it. **The shipped docstring said exactly
that**, then rested the whole feature on one compensating guard: same-pass suppression of an inbound
field outbound is writing. **That guard is structurally unreachable** — per 39c1 the outbound parent op
is never emitted (emit gate skips non-epic parents, bug 8b25; DC's `set_parent` takes only sub-task
children). So the "residual window" the docstring called degraded-pass-only was the NORMAL case.
ONE wrong premise about `managed_refs` produced TWO defects (2b16 and 88d9). On 2b16 an accidental
suppression kept the feature dormant and harmless; here the equivalent guard could never fire, so the
same premise became live data loss.

--- WHAT I DID, IN ORDER (all verified, not assumed) ---
 1. **Disabled `reconcile-bridge`** and cancelled the in-flight pass. It runs every 20 min, had already
    run 5x on the bad code, and would have re-cleared anything repaired.
 2. **Reverted 1288 whole** — change **1292**, now MERGED. Verified on the tree: `diff_inbound_parent`
    is ABSENT from gerrit/main. **Bridge RE-ENABLED on that basis; it is active now.**
 3. **Assessed the damage from the event log**: 63 reconciler-authored `EDIT {"parent_id":""}` events,
    all 63 prior parents recovered from CREATE/SNAPSHOT, all 63 confirmed CURRENTLY parentless (so
    nothing newer could be overwritten), none previously de-parented by a human. Manifest:
    `.claude/jobs/7604559b/tmp/repair.json`.
 4. **Repair**: `rebar edit --parent` REFUSES a closed parent (`_commands/composer.py:503-513`) and 61 of
    63 parents are closed. I checked ALL four candidate routes — no `parent`/`move`/`reparent` verb
    exists, `edit` has NO `--force`, **`rebar revert` does NOT restore state** (`process_revert`
    only appends to `state["reverts"]`; the sole state effect is un-archiving), and `fsck-recover` is
    git-level. **OPERATOR RULING: current state ACCEPTED for the closed tickets; the parent verb is an
    IDEA, out of scope** — filed as `5992-f317-e05e-42f7`. The TWO non-closed victims fell outside that
    acceptance and were repaired with a plain `edit --parent` (no force needed — their parents are still
    open/in_progress): **437c-dd9d-9e65-46e7 -> 9594-1f1c-bcd1-4774, bf03-73bf-b66a-4c84 ->
    4804-d9eb-e682-4d9c**, both verified on the reduced tickets.
 5. **RED TEST FIRST, by operator direction — and it is RED against BOTH wrong states.**
    `test_parent_clear_requires_peer_evidence.py`: the DEFECTIVE tree fails the negative cell ("A local
    parent rebar never pushed was cleared because it is in managed_refs"), the REVERTED tree fails the
    positive cell ("the peer's last-synced parent was DC-9 and the peer now has NONE"). Each wrong state
    satisfies ONE half, so no single assertion separates correct from broken — which is precisely how
    this repo keeps shipping oracles that cannot fail. A third cell holds the fail-open read safe.
 6. **THE FIX: change 1296**, up for review. Adds the evidence `managed_refs` cannot supply —
    `binding_store.get_peer_parent`/`set_peer_parent` (new binding-entry key beside the ADR-0026
    baseline; ABSENT fails safe to NO CLEAR), advanced by `reconcile._advance_peer_parent` from
    `_advance_baselines` **gated on `"parent" in entry`** (the load-bearing line: a fail-open read must
    never overwrite a good observation), and `diff_inbound_parent` declining without it. `managed_refs`
    stays as a further gate but NO LONGER DECIDES. 2079 passed / 1 xfailed across the FULL reconciler
    unit + integration suites; lint, mypy, module-size clean. **Rollout: the first pass after it lands
    clears NOTHING (no observations recorded yet) and self-heals as passes run.**

--- OPERATOR RULINGS THIS SESSION (do not silently re-decide) ---
 * 2b16's certified plan must NOT be implemented as written — I proved its premise false BEFORE
   starting (see #21). Recommendation on record: DEFER (it is a shared-core gap, identical on Cloud,
   and it fails safe). **Still awaiting a decision.**
 * Dedicated `parent` verb with `--force`: IDEA, out of scope (`5992-f317-e05e-42f7`).
 * Store state ACCEPTED for the 61 closed victims; only non-closed ones repaired.
 * "Fix the root cause, but start by adding a RED test" -> done, steps 5-6 above.
 * `binding_store.py` headroom flagged by the operator: it went 749 -> 795, tightened to **787/800**.
   Extraction of the last-synced-peer-state cluster filed as `4522-e600-9e2c-4823` rather than bundled
   into a data-loss fix.

--- NEXT ACTIONS ---
 1. **Land 1296** (needs LLM-Review +1 + Verified +1). Then close 88d9 (`--class preexisting`).
 2. **39c1 SHOULD BE RE-RULED.** It was filed non-gating/borderline. It is now the MECHANISM by which a
    merged change destroyed 63 parent edges — no longer theoretical and demonstrably not fail-safe.
 3. **A FRESH HARNESS RUN IS REQUIRED, and the one from this session is NOT usable.** Run
    **30828166841** completed but ran against `6baa030460` — the DEFECTIVE main — so its
    parent-clear verdicts are meaningless and main has since changed twice (revert + others). **I did
    not read its verdicts; do not tick any 5200 AC off it.** Re-run after 1296 lands:
    `gh workflow run external-integration.yml --repo navapbc/rebar --ref main`, job `jira-dc-harness`.
 4. Then 5200 (18 ACs already verified; it waits only on a run), then e369 (**its plan review is
   `stale-code` — re-run it LAST, immediately before the close**).
 5. 2b16 still needs the operator's build-vs-defer call. If BUILD: the design is the SAME evidence
    channel 1296 just introduced — a per-binding record of what the peer last had — so 1296 is the
    template, and `binding_store` is already a parameter of both link differs.

--- TRAPS PAID FOR THIS SESSION ---
 1. **After a Gerrit submit, the GitHub mirror LAGS.** My first harness dispatch landed on the commit
    BEFORE the merge and nothing in the output would have said so. `git fetch origin main` and confirm
    your commit is on `origin/main` BEFORE dispatching a workflow on `main`.
 2. **A docstring that documents a blind spot is not a mitigation.** 88d9's shipped docstring named the
    exact flaw that destroyed the data and then leaned on a guard nobody checked was reachable. If a
    fix's safety rests on another component firing, GO READ THAT COMPONENT.
 3. `rebar revert` is an AUDIT record, not an undo. Verify before planning a repair around it.
 4. The commit-msg hook rejects a body over 72 cols BEFORE committing (the file stays staged, nothing is
    lost) — and `git commit --amend -F <file>` preserves the Change-Id only if the file CONTAINS the
    Change-Id line. Extract it with `git log -1 --format=%B | grep Change-Id` first.
 5. Running pytest in a worktree with no venv gives `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'rebar'` —
    that is the missing venv on PATH, not a broken tree.
